ai.description: The Meghamalai Rock Gecko reaches 55 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal blotches and a white venter. Distinctive features include a depressed head and enlarged, keeled dorsal tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Hemidactylus vanam* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, sharp, spine-like tubercles along its flanks.
ai.habitat: The Meghamalai Rock Gecko inhabits rocky outcrops and boulders within moist deciduous and evergreen forests at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters in the Western Ghats.
ai.behavior: The Meghamalai rock gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after sunset to forage for small insects on vertical rock faces and trees within its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus vanam* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus vanam* is endemic to the high-elevation rock outcrops of the Meghamalai hills in the Southern Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India.
